point-in-time.title: A feature that existed in event time but was unavailable at prediction time

steps.heading: 10:00 · event
steps.detail: Customer A's transaction count is 5; it arrives at 10:01.

steps.heading: 10:30 · event
steps.detail: The count changes to 8, but its update arrives at 10:45.

steps.heading: 10:35 · prediction
steps.detail: The available feature is still 5. Using 8 here leaks information.

steps.heading: 10:45 · arrival
steps.detail: The delayed update becomes usable for subsequent predictions.

point-in-time.note: An event timestamp alone cannot establish feature availability. Record arrival or publication time as well.

evaluation-path.title: Diagnose a bad answer where it was introduced

steps.heading: Source
steps.detail: Did the document contain the answer, and was its text parsed correctly?

steps.heading: Retrieval
steps.detail: Did the correct evidence reach the candidate set and reranked context?

steps.heading: Generation
steps.detail: Did the model use the provided evidence faithfully?

steps.heading: Action
steps.detail: Did the agent select safe tools and complete the requested operation?

evaluation-path.note: Inspect each stage before attributing the failure to the model.
